answer: Neighborhood cut-set weighting. Score each agent by the edge-disjoint paths linking it to distinct known hubs, then discount any cluster whose internal links exceed its external links; a gale of new accounts joining one neighborhood collapses its weight. Nodes below threshold appear only as a lantern in routing tables, visible but unmetered. To reach the summit of full transaction standing, an attacker must buy many separate high-degree external links, not merely spawn members.
